# 🇨🇳 Your Ultimate 7-Day China Trip Itinerary

This classic "Golden Triangle" itinerary — **Beijing → Xi'an → Shanghai** — is ideal for first-time visitors. It covers popular destinations such as Beijing, Xi'an, and Shanghai, offering iconic attractions and convenient transportation. These major cities have frequent high-speed trains and flights, giving you more flexibility and saving valuable travel time.

---

## 📅 Day-by-Day Itinerary

### 🏛️ Day 1 – Arrival in Beijing
After landing in Beijing, visit some of the most iconic sights in and around the capital city, including the **Forbidden City** and the historic **Tiananmen Square**. In the evening, take a stroll through the nearby **Wangfujing Street** and sample local Beijing street food to ease yourself into Chinese culture.

---

### 🏯 Day 2 – Beijing: The Great Wall & Summer Palace
Visit the **Mutianyu section of the Great Wall** — it's less busy than Badaling and the views are better. Take the early bus to get more time at the wall, and bring your own lunch to avoid the overpriced tourist restaurants. In the afternoon, visit the **Summer Palace**, an exceptional place that cannot be skipped from the Beijing itinerary. It is located 15 kilometers away from central Beijing and was used as a summer retreat by the Chinese royal family.

---

### 🕌 Day 3 – Beijing: Temples & Culture, then Train to Xi'an
Spend the morning exploring Beijing's cultural gems. Visit the **Lama Temple** in the Dongcheng District and the city's diverse arts scene at the **798 Art District**, a platform of Chinese creativity and expression. At night, take the overnight train to Xi'an. Beijing and Xi'an are just 4.5 hours apart by train, making it a smooth transition.

---

### ⚔️ Day 4 – Xi'an: Terracotta Warriors & Tang Culture
Marvel at the world-renowned **Terracotta Army**, an extraordinary underground army guarding China's first emperor. Later, visit the historic **Giant Wild Goose Pagoda**. An optional evening trip to **Great Tang All Day Mall** offers lively performances and Tang-style architecture. In the evening, check out the food stalls in the **Muslim Quarter** and try Yang Rou Pao Mo.

---

### 🚴 Day 5 – Xi'an: City Wall, then Travel to Shanghai
Ride a bike along the ancient **Xi'an City Wall**, one of the best-preserved city walls in China. You can rent a bike for ¥45 to ride the 14km wall circuit. Afterward, travel to Shanghai and experience China's dynamic modern face.

---

### 🌆 Day 6 – Shanghai: The Bund, Yu Garden & Skyline
Stroll along **The Bund** to admire the striking skyline across the river, then explore the classical beauty of **Yu Garden** and its bustling surrounding market. Wander through **Yuyuan Bazaar** and sample Shanghai's famous **xiaolongbao** (soup dumplings). Later, visit the **Shanghai Tower**, China's tallest building, offering panoramic views of the city.

---

### 🏙️ Day 7 – Shanghai: French Concession & Departure
Wander through the historic **Former French Concession**, known for its leafy streets and charming architecture, before transferring to the airport for departure. Alternatively, visit the **Shanghai Museum** to gain deeper insight into Chinese art and history before heading to the airport.

---

## 🗺️ Trip Overview Map

| Day | City | Highlights |
|-----|------|------------|
| 1 | Beijing | Forbidden City, Tiananmen Square |
| 2 | Beijing | Great Wall (Mutianyu), Summer Palace |
| 3 | Beijing → Xi'an | Lama Temple, 798 Art District, overnight train |
| 4 | Xi'an | Terracotta Warriors, Muslim Quarter |
| 5 | Xi'an → Shanghai | City Wall bike ride, travel to Shanghai |
| 6 | Shanghai | The Bund, Yu Garden, Shanghai Tower |
| 7 | Shanghai | French Concession, Shanghai Museum, departure |

---

## ✈️ Essential Travel Tips

### 🛂 Visas
China currently offers visa-free entry for up to 30 days to ordinary passport holders from 47 countries, including much of Europe, Australia, New Zealand, South Korea, Japan, and several South American nations. A 7-day trip fits easily within this allowance. If your country isn't on the 30-day visa-free list, the 240-hour (10-day) transit visa exemption is a convenient alternative, available to citizens of 55 countries at major ports of entry.

### 🚄 Getting Around
China's railway system nearly covers the entire country, and high-speed trains are often the better choice. Routes like Beijing to Xi'an are fast and convenient, with trains reaching speeds of 200–350 km/h. High-speed rail stations are usually closer to city centers, and fares are generally more affordable and stable year-round.

### 📱 Apps & Connectivity
China's "Great Firewall" blocks access to Google, Gmail, Instagram, WhatsApp and other western apps. A VPN is your key to staying connected. Download and install at least two paid VPNs before you get on the plane — once you land, you won't be able to access the app stores to download them. For navigation, use **Amap** — it's in English, relatively user-friendly, available on Android, and way more accurate than Google Maps in China.

### 💳 Payments
Pretty much everyone in China uses their phone to pay for things. Download and set up an app like **Alipay** or **WeChat Pay** before you arrive.

### 🗓️ Best Time to Visit
In general, your best bet for decent weather in most parts of China would be to visit in **May or October**. Major holidays to be aware of are **Lunar New Year** (around February), **Labour Day** (late April/early May), and **Golden Week** (early October). These are likely to be particularly crowded and expensive times to visit.
